subject: Re: Flexi capacity swap & pricing options for mid-contract growth
messages:
From: Emma Clarke <emma@cloudscale.io>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Flex capacity question — need pricing for mid-contract growth

Hi Mateo,

Quick note from CloudScale finance/infra: we expect to increase inference capacity for our recommender by roughly 40% starting mid-December to support a holiday promotion. This is mid-contract — current commit runs through Jan 31, 2027 (co-term).

Two asks:
- Can you outline pricing for (A) a reserved incremental bucket we can add to the commit (12-month billing) vs (B) a one-time top-up voucher that would be billed and draw down over 3 months?
- Any flexibility on discounting for the incremental commit given this is an expansion tied to a product launch? Also curious whether we can align the new capacity to the same co-term without manual proration headaches.

I attached our October usage export to help size the ask. Would like a proposal we can review by EOD Wednesday Nov 11 so procurement can brief execs.

Thanks —
Emma
Emma Clarke
Head of Infrastructure
CloudScale, Inc.
[Attachment: cloudscale_usage_oct2026.csv]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@cloudscale.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Flex capacity question — need pricing for mid-contract growth

Hi Emma — thanks for the data, this helps.

We can support both approaches. High-level options for your team to consider:

1) Incremental reserved bucket (recommended if you want predictable unit economics):
   - Add a dedicated reserved bucket sized for the 40% uplift, with a 12-month addendum that co-terms with your current contract.
   - Pricing: list-rate + a blended uplift discount (we typically offer 8–12% on incremental commits for expansions that size; I will confirm internal approval).

2) Voucher/top-up (recommended for short, bursty growth):
   - One-time voucher invoiced up front; drawdown over a 3-month window. No change to commit or co-term required.
   - Pricing: slightly higher effective per-token rate but lower commitment.

To give you a clean comparison I’ll run a quick workbook (attached) and propose two concrete numeric scenarios. Can we schedule a 20-min sync tomorrow? If procurement needs an expedited path, I can propose a “fast co-term” flow that minimizes proration work.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0142
[Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Workbook_v2.xlsx]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Flex capacity question — need pricing for mid-contract growth

Marissa / Ben — forwarding CloudScale request (below). Customer wants a 40% capacity increase mid-contract (current co-term Jan 31, 2027). They asked for two options: reserved incremental commit vs one-time voucher. Need quick guidance on discount ceilings and whether finance is comfortable with a blended approval if we recommend a commit.

Proposal thoughts from my side: recommend we lead with a reserved addendum at a 12% discount on incremental committed spend if they sign for 12 months (co-term to Jan 31, 2027). Offer an alternative voucher at list less a 5% promotional credit. If approved I’ll prepare an addendum and DocuSign path.

Notes:
- If we co-term to Jan 31, 2027 we should pro-rate the first invoice months and then return to normal monthly billing on Feb 1, 2027.
- Customer timeline: wants decision by EOD Wed Nov 11.

Forwarding the usage CSV for sizing.

— Mateo

> Hi Mateo,
> 
> Quick note from CloudScale finance/infra: we expect to increase inference capacity for our recommender by roughly 40% starting mid-December to support a holiday promotion...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Flex capacity question — need pricing for mid-contract growth

Thanks — finance reviewed. We can approve the following commercial guardrails for this case: 

1) Reserved incremental commit option: up to a 12% discount on incremental committed spend for a 12-month addendum co-terming to Jan 31, 2027. Finance prefers a straight 10% floor unless AE can justify higher on ARR/strategic rationale. For CloudScale (large infra customer + potential expansion) I’m comfortable authorizing up to 12% with Marissa sign-off.

2) Voucher/top-up option: allowed at list less a 5% promotional credit (no change to commit).

3) One-time onboarding credit (to help cover migration overhead): $25,000 credit if they commit to the 12-month addendum and sign the co-term. Credit applies to the first invoice after DocuSign completion.

4) Billing mechanics: we will pro-rate the incremental commit to co-term date (prorated first invoice), then invoice on normal monthly cadence. Finance will add a short appendix to the addendum clarifying proration math.

If Marissa approves the 12% endorsement, you can proceed to prepare the addendum and DocuSign request.

— Ben
[Attachment: pricing_calc.pdf]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@cloudscale.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Flex capacity question — need pricing for mid-contract growth

Hi Emma — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review we can offer two concrete paths:

A) Reserved incremental commit (recommended)
   - Size: +40% reserved bucket (sized per your usage file).
   - Term: addendum co-terming to Jan 31, 2027 (12-month billing on the new capacity).
   - Commercial: 12% discount on the incremental committed spend (we can approve up to 12% for this account).
   - Credit: $25,000 onboarding credit applied to first invoice after DocuSign.
   - Billing: first invoice will be prorated to co-term date; thereafter normal monthly billing.

B) Voucher / short-term top-up
   - One-time voucher invoiced up front, drawdown over 3 months; effectively higher per-token rate but no added commit.
   - Commercial: list less 5% promotional credit. No onboarding credit for voucher.

Next steps: I attached the addendum and the numeric workbook. If this looks good I’ll send the addendum via DocuSign and schedule a 20-min call to walk procurement through the proration appendix.
